name: Topper Site
hook: A South Carolina chert quarry where pieces in sediment over 50,000 years old may be tools or natural breaks.
claim: In November 2004 Albert Goodyear announced radiocarbon ages of at least 50,300 years on burnt plant remains from deep in a Pleistocene river terrace at Topper, where his team found stone pieces he considered tools -- an extension of pre-Clovis finds made there since 1998.

claimed_age.label: ≥50,300 14C BP (minimum age)
claimed_age.basis: Two radiocarbon dates, 50,300 and 51,700 14C BP (uncalibrated), on burnt plant remains, UC Irvine lab; the dater said the absolute age is not known. bp_min is the proponents' 'at least 50,000 years'.

orthodoxy_at_claim.label: Pre-Clovis Monte Verde (~14,500 cal BP) had been accepted in 1997 (S11); no New World claim over 40,000 years had survived professional scrutiny (S10).

unambiguous_signal.note: Stone pieces at a chert quarry. Michael Collins, who had seen them, called them geofacts; specialists awaited study of human versus natural origin.

documented_context.note: Dug ~4 m into the Pleistocene terrace by backhoe and hand. Of three samples from the dated level, one was modern and attributed to an intrusion, so the level was not sealed.

multiple_dating_methods.note: Only radiocarbon dated the deep level; the OSL dates in S9's timeline are on soils above 'ice age strata' (pre-Clovis 'older than 14,000').

multiple_labs.note: Both finite dates came from one lab (UC Irvine), on samples Stafford collected. The lab for the ≥3 earlier >50,000-year dates (S10) is not stated.

professional_recovery.note: Excavated by Goodyear's SCIAA team (Allendale PaleoIndian Expedition, with public volunteers), by backhoe and hand; Stafford collected the dated samples.

peer_reviewed_report.note: Announced by press release; Anderson awaited formal publication (S10). Goodyear's 2005 chapter covers only ~12,000-16,000 RCYBP evidence. S1 (2009) unread.

material_accessible.note: Outside geologists led by Waters worked at the site from 1999 (S9), and critic Michael Collins had seen the pieces by 2004 (S10).

independent_teams.note: Outside geologists led by Waters (Texas A&M) studied and dated the site's soils from 1999, alongside the project; they published separately in 2009 (S1).

proponent_stake.note: No commercial, religious or nationalist motive documented. Goodyear was a USC research archaeologist at SCIAA (since 1974) and founder of the Allendale PaleoIndian Expedition.

objections.text: The stone pieces from the dated level are natural fractures (geofacts), not human-made tools.
objections.raised_by: Michael Collins, Univ. of Texas (2004); Waters et al. 2009 UNVERIFIED
objections.outcome_note: Proponents still describe a core-and-flake industry in the terrace (S2, 2018); no study settling human versus natural origin was found in the sources read.

objections.text: Earlier New World claims over 40,000 years had not survived professional examination, so the dates need careful verification and reporting in scientific journals.
objections.outcome_note: No proponents' journal report of the ≥50,300 dates was found in the sources read; Goodyear's 2005 chapter (S8) covers younger pre-Clovis evidence only.

objections.text: One of three samples from the dated level gave a modern age, attributed to an intrusion, so the level was not sealed and the pieces' association with the dated carbon is uncertain.
objections.raised_by: Intrusive date reported by T. Stafford (2004)
objections.outcome_note: ARCHAEOLOGY (S10) expected the context to face close scrutiny; no micromorphology or refit study of this level was found in the sources read.

objections.text: The dates show only that the material is at least 50,300 radiocarbon years old; its absolute age is not known.
objections.outcome_note: The dater's own caveat; ≥3 earlier dates on the lower soils were also beyond 50,000 years (S10). Not disputed in the sources read.

status_note: Dates from the level are minimum ages only (≥50,300 14C BP). Collins (2004) judged the pieces geofacts; the proponents still present a pre-LGM occupation in the terrace (S2, 2018). Human origin remains unsettled.

timeline.event: Goodyear's team digs up to a meter below the Clovis level and finds unusual stone pieces up to two meters below the surface.
Outside geologists led by Michael Waters (Texas A&M) visit and propose a full geological study of the site.
Geologists take plant remains deep in the Pleistocene terrace; OSL on soils above 'ice age strata' puts pre-Clovis at over 14,000 years.
May: backhoe and hand excavation reaches ~4 m below the surface in the terrace; T. Stafford collects charcoal from a black stain where pieces lay.
November: Goodyear announces dates of 50,300 and 51,700 14C BP (UC Irvine); a third sample is modern, attributed to an intrusion.
Michael Collins, who had seen the pieces, calls them geofacts; David Anderson and others await formal publication.
Goodyear reviews four eastern pre-Clovis sites, Topper included, at ~12,000-16,000 RCYBP; the abstract does not mention the 50k dates.
Waters, Forman, Stafford & Foss publish a geoarchaeological study of Topper and Big Pine Tree; Waters' team had worked there since 1999.
Goodyear & Sain maintain a pre-LGM pre-Clovis core-and-flake occupation (Clariant complex) in the Pleistocene terrace.
Jennings et al. report a probable Clovis hearth and domestic structure, part of Topper's separate Clovis occupation.

decisive_tests.test: Date the sands of the artifact-bearing terrace level by luminescence (OSL/IRSL) for a finite burial age, after checking whether S1 already reports such ages.
decisive_tests.would_show: A finite age for the level, which the radiocarbon minimum ages (≥50,300 14C BP) cannot give.

decisive_tests.test: Blind test: lithic specialists sort the terrace pieces mixed with chert fragments collected from sterile terrace sediment, without knowing which is which.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether the claimed tools can be told apart from natural breakage in the same deposit.

decisive_tests.test: Micromorphology on any archived sediment from the 2004 black stain, or on a newly exposed equivalent stain in the same terrace level.
decisive_tests.would_show: Whether the burnt layer is an in-place human combustion feature or natural burning or root staining, and whether intrusions cut it.

decisive_tests.test: Use-wear and residue analysis at high magnification on pieces from the dated level, with naturally broken chert from the same terrace as controls.
decisive_tests.would_show: Edge wear or organic residues that natural fracture would not produce.

falsifier: Refuted if blind analysis finds the terrace pieces indistinguishable from naturally broken chert in sterile terrace sediment. Supported if pieces sealed in the dated level show use-wear or residues natural breakage cannot make, and finite luminescence ages confirm its age.

confidence_note: Key facts rest on two 2004 reports read directly (S9, S10) and abstracts (S2, S8, S11). S1, the main external study, is unread (paywalled), so none of its findings are used.
notes: Scope: only the 2004 finds deep in the Pleistocene terrace. Pre-Clovis finds of 1998-2003 lay above the terrace, in soils outside geologists dated to ~16,000 years (S9, S10); the Clovis occupation (S4, S7) is separate. Stafford both collected the 2004 samples (S9) and co-authored S1. S1 could not be read (paywalled; open copies blocked), so reports that it doubts the human origin of the sub-Clovis pieces come only from search summaries: UNVERIFIED. Sources differ on Stafford's affiliation: Stafford Laboratories, Boulder (S9) vs University of Wisconsin (S10). The expedition includes public volunteers under professional direction (S9).

open_issues: S1 (Waters et al. 2009) still unread: no abstract in OpenAlex; publisher, Academia and ResearchGate copies return HTTP 403. Kept at 'exists'; the 'unchanged tools' objection was removed and Waters' critic role is marked UNVERIFIED.
Declined in part: Waters et al. (2009) not added to status_note or as a confirmed raiser of the geofact objection, since S1 could not be read; kept only as UNVERIFIED in raised_by and in key_critics.
peer_reviewed_report coded 'no' rather than 'partial': whether S1 reports the ≥50,300 dates is unknown. Recode to 'partial' if S1 is shown to treat them.
Declined: confidence 'low' until S1 is read. Set 'medium' because no field now relies on S1 or on Wikipedia; key facts rest on two contemporary reports read directly.
Removed for lack of a readable source: the 1985 SCIAA excavation, the 1998 flood detail and the natural-fire objection (the Goodyear 2005 PDF returns HTTP 403).
S8 editors and publisher come from the prior draft (a 2008 American Antiquity review); this revision confirmed only title, author, venue, year and pages.
Objection [2] (intrusion) is framed from Stafford's own report of a modern intrusive date and ARCHAEOLOGY's call for context scrutiny; no named critic made this exact argument in the sources read.

D19 re-rating 2026-09-23: unchanged — open fits, borderline unsupported: tool-vs-geofact is argued both ways (2004, 2018) and nothing was withdrawn, but the ≥50,300 14C BP dates are minimum ages and no journal report of them was found.
